title: The memory consolidator is told which models read the file it rewrites
objective: The consolidator's prompt (and its peer's) lists the models that read the memory file, taken from the config, and asks it to size and phrase the file for them, with no length cap.
outline: devloop/core/memory.py: READERS = {'creator': ('creator',), 'worker': ('worker', 'worker_simple'), 'verifier': ('verifier',), 'reviewer': ('reviewer',), 'fixer': ('fixer',)} next to ROLES (these are the roles whose prompts call for_prompt: ticket_creator, ticket_issuer, auto_fixer; no prompt reads role/consolidator.md); readers(cfg, layer, name) and a readers_section(cfg, layer, name) text helper (core/agents.py does not import memory, so importing model_of is safe; a local import is fine too). devloop/memory_keeper.py _keep(): values['readers'] = the section text; discuss() already passes values through (peer_values and the revised prompt are dict(values, ...)). prompts/consolidator.md: replace the first paragraph's 'Every agent that starts ...' sentences with the {readers} section; prompts/consolidator_peer.md: the same {readers} section before '## The file before'. Do not touch quota_hook (#149 edits it).
test_plan: Verifier owns items 1-5, in tests_devloop/test_memory.py as class T<N>Acceptance placed between the existing classes KeeperInterrupt and MemoryFolderHelpers. Fixture: self.config(agents={...}) with each role's commands being the fake agent with a distinct --model (the fake ignores its arguments; model_of reads --model): creator [['python3', AGENT[1], '--model', 'm-creator']], worker [[..., 'm-w1'], [..., 'm-w2']], worker_simple [[..., 'm-ws'], [..., 'm-w1']], verifier [[..., 'm-v']], reviewer [[..., 'm-r']], fixer [[..., 'm-f']], consolidator and consolidator_peer [[..., 'm-c']]. memory_keeper writes no prompt when no lesson waits, so queue at least one lesson for the file under test through the pool (as T15Acceptance.queue writes memory/inbox rows), then run memory_keeper.py: --layer role --name worker -> bullets exactly ['- m-w1', '- m-w2', '- m-ws']; --layer role --name creator -> ['- m-creator']; --layer model --name m-v -> ['- m-v']; --layer project --name project -> ['- m-creator', '- m-w1', '- m-w2', '- m-ws', '- m-v', '- m-r', '- m-f']; --layer role --name consolidator -> ['- no agent's prompt includes this file']; the item-3 sentence present and the item-4 sentence absent; with unlimited_tokens true and the peer's default verdict 'change', peer/prompt.md and revised/prompt.md have the worker bullets. Expected lists come from this ticket. Implementer's unit tests for readers() (between LessonsHelpers and Memory). Seconds each.
notes: Source: plan item 3.7 (D-101), docs/HANDOFF.md last section (D-100, D-101, D-102): the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from T's main session (T is another project that runs agent-control daily, 2026-11-26). Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Refer to T only as 'another project' in code, tests and comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids its name in every non-markdown file) and copy no path from these notes into code. D-101 (user's words: 「記憶的長短請llm依據目標的模型自己做調整」): no fixed length cap; the consolidating LLM sizes the file by who reads it and must be given that. Read in code: memory.for_prompt(cfg, role, model) puts the role file and the model file of the chain's first command into the prompt once; whichever command of the chain then runs reads it, so a role file reaches every model of the chain (worker and worker_simple share role/worker.md: ticket_issuer.start passes role 'worker' for both); no prompt includes role/consolidator.md; project.md is given by path to the creator, worker, verifier, reviewer and fixer prompts. Not measured: how much shorter files get. Group new-g1 (phase-one group 3; touches no open ticket's code: #149 edits only quota_hook in memory_keeper.py).
acceptance: devloop/core/memory.py has readers(cfg, layer, name) returning the distinct model names (agents.model_of of each command, chain order, first appearance kept) of: role 'creator' -> the creator chain; role 'worker' -> the worker chain, then the worker_simple chain (cfg.agent_chain, which falls back to worker when worker_simple is unset); roles 'verifier', 'reviewer', 'fixer' -> their own chains; any other role name -> []; layer 'model' -> [name]; layer 'project' -> the creator, worker, worker_simple, verifier, reviewer and fixer chains in that order.

The prompt memory_keeper.py gives the consolidator (runs/memory/<layer>-<name>-*/prompt.md) has a section headed exactly '## Who reads this file' whose bullet lines (lines starting '- ' up to the next '## ' heading) are exactly '- <model>' for each name readers() returns, in order; when it returns [], the only bullet is exactly '- no agent's prompt includes this file'.

That section says that for role and model files these readers get the whole file in every prompt, and for the project file that they read it when their work touches it (their prompts give its path); it contains the sentence 'Size and phrase the file for these readers; there is no length cap.'

devloop/prompts/consolidator.md no longer contains 'Every agent that starts in this role or on this model reads this file, so every line costs every session.'; its '## What belongs in each layer' section is unchanged.

With devloop.unlimited_tokens true, the peer's prompt (runs/memory/<...>/peer/prompt.md, from consolidator_peer.md) has the same '## Who reads this file' section with the same bullets, and so has the consolidator's second prompt (revised/prompt.md) when the peer asks for changes.

devloop/README.md '## Memory' gains one sentence: the consolidator is told the file's readers (the models of the role's command chains in the config, the model itself for a model file, the reading roles' models for project.md) and sizes the file for them, with no length cap (D-101); the phrases test_memory.T19Acceptance.test_item3_memory_section checks stay, and none of the phrases it forbids appears.
token_basis: a small helper in core/memory.py, one value in memory_keeper.py, two prompt files and a README sentence, one fixture and five keeper runs with fake agents; simple tickets with a verifier landed at 1.1M-2.0M recorded
vision: 記憶 (VISION: layered memory that keeps improving; D-101) for 每張落地票的 token (down) and 一次就過測試的比例 (up): every agent prompt carries its role and model memory, so a file sized for the models that read it costs less per run and reads better for a smaller model; size of the effect not measured.

request:
# Phase one, group 3: fewer tokens, fewer wasted rounds (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-101, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 3.1-3.7)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26); write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data. Read docs/VISION.md; each ticket names its metric and what it removes. Tests in the area's own file in tests_devloop/ with loop_harness.py; seconds each. Open tickets in groups g12-g14 (#142-#151) are running; depend on them where you touch the same code.

## 3.1 The code index lists test files by path only
Measured on A: CODE-MAP.md is 209,241 bytes; tests/ and tests_devloop/ sections are 151,110 (72.2%). The worker and verifier prompts say "read it before searching"; the fixer gets it too. devloop/core/codemap.py's docstring says tests are listed by path only, but build() expands them. T's test files are larger.
Wanted: files under the project's test roots (tests.unittest.roots) and test_*.py files get one path line. Add tests_devloop/test_codemap.py (none exists). Check agent logs (runs/*/agent-*.log) whether agents read the index whole, and write what you found. Whether to drop module-level `_` functions too: measure and decide.

## 3.2 The opener knows the hard_block rules before it writes a plan
T (seen there): #369 and #375 had test plans using os.kill; the tickets hit hard_block only after the work was done, waited for the user, were revised, and a round was wasted. The opener's prompt has no hard_block (main session, read the code).
Wanted: the project's hard_block (paths, dirs, patterns) is in the opener's prompt with what it means (a ticket whose change matches stops before merge for the user). The hand-in check refuses (one retry, like other field checks) a ticket whose outline, test_plan or acceptance contains a hard_block pattern unless the ticket says, in a dedicated field or line, that it needs the user's approval at merge and why.

## 3.3 After a revision the next round reads the new ticket
T (seen there): after #320 was revised, the round-2 worker got the text from before the revision and reported the same conflict again.
Wanted: reproduce it first with the loop harness (revise with `actl new --revise` while a round is running; see what the next round's prompt holds). Fix it so the next round always reads the revised ticket. A running round whose work the revision changed is stopped and counts as a free round (like a revision that voids the cases).

## 3.4 A worker does not run the reviser itself
T (seen there): workers running under agy's account environment (HOME replaced) called the revise command; claude could not read its login and agy.sh resolved wrong paths; it failed several times. devloop/prompts/worker.md tells the worker to run {revise_cmd} itself.
Wanted: as for `blocked` hand-ins (#113): the worker hands in "revise" with its reason; the issuer runs the opener outside the agent's environment. REVISED -> the next round with the new ticket; UNCHANGED -> the next round with the opener's answer attached; ESCALATED -> a page as today. The verifier uses the same path. Removes: an agent starting another agent inside its own environment.

## 3.5 Automatic fix tickets go into the next group that has not started verifying
T (seen there): g90, g91, g92 were each one or two flaky-fix tickets and each ran a full regression (about 75 minutes in T).
Wanted: when the controller opens a ticket by itself (flaky, release red), the request asks the opener to put it into a group of the chain that has not started its regression, and to open a new group only when none fits; the opener's group rule (prompts/creator/02-rules.md) says the same.

## 3.6 The opener's prompt carries only the live part of the DAG
Measured: A's opener prompt is 25 KB and includes all of dag.json, landed tickets too; T has about 400 tickets.
Wanted: the copy put into t
